summary: tslint-folder-schema preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute bundled obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares `scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs"`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts it to a temp directory, and then uses that freshly downloaded runtime to execute a sibling file `math_init.js` via `execFileSync`. math_init.js is a ~727 KB heavily obfuscated blob (string-array + rotation shuffler `WV8StW`, hex-named identifiers such as `MmgoCP` / `etDiOOB`, no comments or readable symbols). The advertised purpose is a TSLint folder-schema rule (`main: lib/folderSchemaRule.js` with tslint/lodash/commander dependencies) and the small lib file is a plausible-looking lint rule; nothing about that purpose requires Bun or a 727 KB opaque module. README is a `TODO` placeholder and the declared homepage points to an unrelated repository. The Bun runtime is used specifically to execute code that would otherwise be inspected by standard Node-based install-time scanners, and the executed payload's contents cannot be resolved statically. Installing this package causes an alternate runtime to be fetched and used to run attacker-controlled obfuscated code on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
